newsitem.title: USA: Cel-Sci cleared to test Multikine.
newsitem.headline: Cel-Sci cleared to test Multikine.

text.p: Cel-Sci Corp said Monday the U.S. Food and Drug Administration has given clearance to start human testing of the company's Multikine in HIV infected individuals in West Hollywood, Calif.
The phase I trial is expected to start in the first quarter to evaluate safety and monitor for improvement in immune responses in HIV infected individuals.
The clinical trial will be conducted by Aids Research Alliance, a non-profit AIDS research organization located in West Hollywood, Calif.

"Although recent advances have been made in the treatment of HIV/AIDS utilizing anti-retroviral drugs, we have a long way to go until HIV disease can be considered 'manageable' or curable," explained Aids Research chief executive Gregory Britt.

"Therapies which help to correct the immune system dysregulation caused by HIV are urgently needed. It is believed that immune-based therapies in combination with anti-retroviral drugs could be the one-two punch that is needed to successfully knock out HIV/AIDS."

Multikine is a mixture of human immune system regulators called cytokines. It contains Interleukin-2 and other cytokines, several of which are being investigated individually as potential HIV-1 and cancer treatments. Multikine is currently being tested in patients with head and neck cancer and prostate cancer, Cel-Sci said.
